## Reading and Benchmarking an Inference Deployment {#sec-ch7}

::: {.callout-note title="Scaffold status"}
Scaffold only: drafting has not yet begun. This page records the approved plan for the chapter; it contains no teaching content, questions, answers, figures, worked examples or citations yet.
:::

**Purpose.** Apply the workbook's definitions to specify a fair benchmark and to read deployment and performance claims critically.

**Prerequisites and planned recap.** Workbook 05 Chapter 6 (configured, observed and derived numbers); Chapter 1 (metric contract), Chapter 3 (SLO attainment) and Chapter 4 (kernel versus end-to-end).

**Scope boundaries.** The workbook runs no benchmark. Warm-up and open- versus closed-loop load guidance is the workbook's own methodology, not a source claim.

### Learning objectives

Planned outcomes (approved scope). By the end of this chapter you should be able to:

- Specify a benchmark: model, hardware, precision, length distributions, arrival process, concurrency, warm-up and percentiles.
- Map a reported metric to its definition.
- Separate kernel, engine and end-to-end claims.
- Read a published deployment description and label each number reported, derived or illustrative.
